key_insight: A GPT2 table-to-text approach can outperform traditional ML and neural networks on small, imbalanced clinical datasets by leveraging contextual clinical reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This suggests a potential way to improve disease risk prediction from limited structured healthcare data while keeping outputs more clinically interpretable.
method: Converted structured patient records into physician-style text.
Used GPT4-generated paraphrasing to augment minority-class examples.
Fine-tuned GPT2 on four public healthcare datasets and applied gradient-based explainability.
evidence_signal: Across heart disease, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, and thyroid cancer recurrence datasets, the model reported average precision, specificity, sensitivity, and F1-score of 0.96, 0.97, 0.96, and 0.96.
watch_item: The results are based on public low-volume datasets, so external validation and careful checks for synthetic-text bias are needed before real-world deployment.
paper_title: Can GPT Be Used as an Alternative Prediction Model to Traditional Machine Learning and Neural Networks on Low-Volume Clinical Data?
